To mitigate these, they propose 'everlasting repetition'—a term suggesting infinite trials under identical conditions. Mathematically, this maps to a convergence proof: as repetition approaches infinity, the probability of catastrophic behavioral deviation tends toward zero, assuming ergodicity within the system. However, human cognition introduces non-linearities; impulsiveness suppression acts as a bounded stochastic process, while coaching discipline enforces Dirichlet boundary conditions on formation states. Together, they create a feedback loop stabilizing team dynamics around optimal baselines. Dualities emerge: repetition versus spontaneity, protocol versus performance. Failure occurs when impulsivity overwhelms discipline, leading to catastrophic state transitions.
